objective: Audit SuperEzio pipeline component-by-component (config, math, gateway, DataHub, expert isolation), fix confirmed defects with evidence, no feature invention beyond documented gaps.
what_was_done: Phase 1: audited config/runtime.yml, .env.example, providers.py, math_hub.py. Confirmed context_length 4096 vs 65536 contradiction against .f51/ENTRYPOINT_MAP.md; confirmed .env.example had 3 duplicated variables; confirmed math_hub._quantum_module used numpy RandomState(42) fixed seed; confirmed f51_module used consensus=0.65 hardcoded constant.

Phase 2: audited gateway.py end-to-end. Confirmed allow_fallback existed only on stream_generate_async, not on the sync path (generate/chat_completion) that expert_dialogue.py actually calls — silent provider fallback (including Gemini as an orphaned fallback target) could not be disabled during research runs.

Phase 3: audited data_hub.py. Confirmed DataHub._is_usable_result treats an empty dict {} as a usable result (only checks absence of 'error' key), which would silently break the market-data fallback chain if any provider ever returns {}.

Phase 4: audited expert data isolation. Confirmed all 6 named experts, red team, judge, and auditor received the identical unfiltered data_context (raw math_report + message) with zero filtering — contradicting the intended architecture where each expert sees only its relevant data and the judge arbitrates expert verdicts rather than re-reading raw market data.

Researched TradingAgents (Xiao et al., arXiv:2412.20138, TauricResearch), FinRobot (AI4Finance-Foundation, arXiv:2405.14767), and AIMM (arXiv:2512.16103) for real multi-agent financial system role/prompt/data-isolation patterns.
Fixed math_hub.py: _quantum_module now derives its Monte Carlo seed from the actual quantum walk counts (sha256 hash) instead of a hardcoded 42.

Fixed math_hub.py: _f51_module now computes real consensus from expert_results when available (Counter over parsed verdicts), falls back to a documented neutral 0.5 with consensus_is_heuristic=true when no experts have run yet (was: silent 0.65 constant always).

Fixed gateway.py + expert_dialogue.py: added allow_fallback param end-to-end on the sync path (generate -> chat_completion), plus gateway.last_provider_used tracking. expert_dialogue.py now forces allow_fallback=False when SUPEREZIO_RESEARCH_PAPER_ONLY or SUPEREZIO_DAYTRADE_PAPER_ONLY is set, and records provider_used + fallback_occurred in every expert result.

Fixed experts.py: added EXPERT_CONTEXT_MODULES (role -> allowed math_report module names) and build_role_context() to slice math_report per role instead of sending the full report to everyone. Added build_judge_context() so judge/auditor roles receive a structured summary of expert verdicts instead of raw market data. Rewrote all 6 EXPERT_PROMPTS with an anti-guessing contract (declare NO_DATA instead of inventing numbers) and explicit references to which real-system role each SuperEzio expert mirrors.

Documented (did not guess) the runtime.yml context_length/gpu_layers divergence against ENTRYPOINT_MAP.md with an inline comment — verified via disk check that neither referenced GGUF model exists on this machine (C:\llama.cpp\ absent), so neither number can be trusted without a live server measurement.
Cleaned 3 duplicated env var entries in .env.example.
RISK_REGISTER.md INV-R4 (4 leaked API keys in git history) updated: operator explicitly and knowingly accepted the risk without rotation on 2026-07-18 — recorded verbatim, not a technical decision.
Committed all changes locally as 7f77357 (disk-only per .f51/GITHUB_POLICY.json — no git push/pull/fetch performed at any point).
